reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a step-by-step Blogger tutorial covering account navigation, theme selection, post creation, publication controls, and applying for monetization. Although it discusses earning money and gives an income figure, it states that results are not typical or guaranteed and does not describe a request for payment, credentials, or private data. The potentially inaccurate copyright-related statement does not establish a deceptive mechanism.

That's it friends, we successfully created our blogger account
you can also click on confirm & you blog post will be posted on google
They will give you some amount to be invested by monetize your blog post

opening.argument: The video ties a low-effort action directly to a specific monetary outcome. It asks viewers to use a “simple method” and says Google can produce Rs 31,000 per month for free, requiring only a phone. The proposed path is not merely general education: viewers are directed to Blogger, told to select a Gmail account, create and publish a blog, and apply for monetization. The account-selection step is presented as connected to where money will be sent, while monetization is said to provide an amount. That is a concrete promise-action chain: follow the setup and publishing steps, then pursue the claimed Google income. The fact that the steps involve a real blogging interface does not substantiate the promised return.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The existence of Blogger controls does not answer the central issue: whether the promised income is actually linked to the recommended actions. The defense describes navigation but leaves unexplained why the video presents Rs 31,000 per month as attainable through a free, simple method, or why account selection is described in terms of receiving money. Calling the process a tutorial does not remove its solicitation-like monetary framing.

citations.quote: is it possible to reach out the amount from google to get Rs 31,000 per month
You can create your own business with Google platform and use the money we have from Google as revenue

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material does not show that Google promises or pays the stated amount. The Blogger steps establish only account creation, content production, and an application for monetization; they do not establish approval, payment, or a guaranteed result. The language about money is an imprecise explanation of possible monetization, not evidence of a deceptive payment flow.

citations.quote: That's it friends, we successfully created our blogger account
There is NO guarantee that you will earn any money using the techniques and ideas mentioned in this video.

opening.argument: Several red flags appear together: a concrete monthly figure, an allegedly free method, minimal effort, and instructions to create online content before seeking monetization. The speaker says the method is completely free and needs only a phone, yet also presents a path to Rs 31,000 per month. The promised ease is reinforced by claims that most of the work is already complete after basic setup and that the remaining work is simple. Even without a deposit request, this is the characteristic low-barrier-income pitch: substantial returns are made to sound accessible through routine clicks and posts. A disclaimer cannot make those promotional impressions reliable, especially where the video supplies no substantiation for the figure.

you need what all in the first two phases these have many of your advcnce settings
Any earnings or income statements, or any earnings or income examples, are only estimates of what we think you could earn.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the disclaimer as dispositive, but the video’s dominant message still combines a precise income figure with “free,” phone-only participation and a simple workflow. A caveat that results are not guaranteed does not explain the basis for the figure or prevent viewers from being led to expect it. Nor does the presence of ordinary interface screens resolve the unsupported earnings implication.

When we applied before 3 years , I only added 10 post after that after I applied, they instantly did the application and they got the approval by Google

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The risk framing overstates what the evidence proves. The video expressly disclaims guaranteed earnings and describes work, content creation, and Google review rather than automatic payment. The Rs 31,000 statement is not accompanied by a deposit, fee, purchase, or promise that every viewer will receive it; the quoted simplicity describes blog setup, not guaranteed income.

citations.quote: There is NO guarantee that you will earn any money using the techniques and ideas mentioned in this video.
Your level of success in attaining the results claimed in this video will require hard-work, experience, and knowledge.

opening.argument: Although the video is presented as instruction, its practical function is to promote participation in a purported Google income opportunity. It opens with the prospect of earning Rs 31,000 per month, then moves viewers through the account, blog, posting, and monetization route. It also asks viewers to subscribe, like, share, and comment about their interests, and later offers personal contact through Instagram. Those engagement and contact prompts surround the income pitch and encourage viewers to enter the proposed workflow rather than merely understand blogging. The educational format therefore increases credibility for a promotional claim: a screen-recorded tutorial makes the opportunity look operational while leaving the earnings premise unverified.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense’s description of tutorial topics is incomplete because it omits the surrounding acquisition language: the viewer is first presented with a monthly income opportunity, prompted to engage with the channel, and invited to contact the speaker. Demonstrating Blogger features can function as credibility-building support for that opportunity. The absence of a fee does not make the income promotion non-soliciting when participation and contact are actively encouraged.

citations.quote: if you try to use the simple method as mentioned in this video, Google can do it for you from Google for free
you can contact me as much as your wish.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The engagement prompts promote the channel, not a paid scheme, and the Instagram invitation is for questions about several topics. The tutorial visibly and verbally explains Blogger creation, themes, posts, images, and publication. None of the cited prompts asks viewers to pay, transfer funds, surrender credentials, or join a recruitment structure, so promotional presentation alone does not establish a scam mechanism.
